name: Status pills
description: A compact, read-only label that communicates the current state of a resource or operation.

props.name: Label
props.description: Required, explicit state in sentence case. Prefer one to three words. Unknown values must have a meaningful fallback label.

props.name: Tone
props.description: Semantic role chosen from the state's meaning in its domain. Never infer it from the label alone.

props.name: Size
props.description: Small for rows and dense lists; Medium for resource headers and summaries.

props.name: Icon
props.description: Optional leading semantic icon. It supplements the label and uses the same foreground color.

props.name: Surface
props.description: Choose the foreground/background pair for the surface behind the pill.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Content-sized, borderless pill with a soft semantic fill, full radius, no border or shadow. Horizontal inline-flex, items centered, 4px gap between icon and label. Width follows content; minimum height grows when a translated label wraps.

anatomy.name: LeadingIcon
anatomy.description: Optional semantic icon, 12x12 in both Small and Medium, matching the label's font size. Same foreground color as the label. Decorative to assistive technology (aria-hidden). Hidden by default.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Required state label. Open Sans, 12px / 16px, weight 600 at both sizes. Keep the complete status visible, including words such as 'not' or 'failed'.

icons.note: Icon set used by the documentation preview; the spec only requires a check, warning, error, or progress symbol that reinforces the state without replacing the words.

notes: Text and icon share the foreground token; the container uses the background token. Use each light or dark pair together.
Contrast values are computed with the site's own contrastRatio() formula (WCAG relative luminance) from the resolved hex pairs. All ten pairs exceed 4.5:1.
Documentation surfaces behind the pill: light examples sit on --flowx-grays-50 (#ffffff) or --flowx-neutrals-50 (#f7f8f9); dark examples sit on --flowx-neutrals-900 (#1d232c).

Neutral.meaning: A passive state with no immediate action.

Info.meaning: Work is progressing or a transition is underway.

Success.meaning: An operation succeeded or a resource is ready.

Warning.meaning: Attention or a decision is needed to continue.

Danger.meaning: An operation failed or access was denied.

guidelines.title: Use the same meaning in every view
guidelines.description: A migration that is in progress keeps its blue Info tone in the table and in the resource header. Size can change with density; meaning cannot.

guidelines.title: Separate ongoing work from attention
guidelines.description: Use Info for normal processing. Reserve Warning for a condition that needs intervention, such as an import waiting at an approval gate.

guidelines.title: Keep context in the label
guidelines.description: 'Active' can mean an enabled account or a token still executing. Map the domain state first: the account is Success; the executing token is Info. Never use a universal keyword-to-color lookup.

guidelines.title: A pill describes; an action sits beside it
guidelines.description: Keep status pills read-only with a default cursor. Use a separate button for Retry, Review, or Enable. Hover, pressed, selected, and disabled interaction styles do not apply to a status label.

guidelines.title: Keep passive states visually quiet
guidelines.description: Use Neutral for drafts, queued work, or intentionally inactive resources. A disabled account remains an explicit domain decision: blocked access may need Danger, while an intentionally disabled configuration can stay Neutral.

guidelines.title: Always keep the words
guidelines.description: Color and icons reinforce a visible label. Do not replace a status with a colored dot, a checkmark alone, or a tooltip. Use a full label for unknown states and preserve the source value in the details.

guidelines.title: Choose the pair for the surface
guidelines.description: Use the paired light or dark foreground and background tokens together. Dark-surface colors are part of this proposal; the product does not yet have a shared dark pill contract.

guidelines.title: Keep other badge roles separate
guidelines.description: Build versions, branch names, environments, counters, and removable filter chips describe identity, quantity, or selection. Do not assign them success or warning meaning just because they have a pill-shaped container.

accessibility.role: Static text (span). Use a separate role="status" live region only for meaningful asynchronous updates.
keyboard: Tab skips the pill. Put any adjacent action in its own keyboard-focusable button or link.
aria: aria-hidden="true" on the decorative icon; the visible label carries the meaning.
aria-live="polite": announce a meaningful change once in a dedicated status region, not on every pill in a table.
accessibility.longLabels: Keep the complete state visible. Let the pill grow vertically when necessary; do not truncate critical status text.
accessibility.motion: A static progress icon is sufficient. If an implementation animates it, honor reduced-motion preferences.

adoptionNotes: Current tags mix solid fills, soft fills, and six corner treatments. This proposal standardizes status on a soft, full-radius pill. Build tags, branch chips, environments, and counters keep their distinct roles.

Migration progress is Warning in tables and Info in headers. Process Started and active tokens also use Warning. Move normal ongoing work to Info consistently; keep Warning for a blocked or attention-needed condition.

The shared status wrapper uses Neutral for Info, while soft tags use Blue. Its 500-level foregrounds also differ from this proposal's darker text. Adopt the paired tokens together across pills and status cells.

Runtime content currently uses different green shades and an 8px radius. Clearing is red in that screen: review that domain's destructive-operation meaning before changing it to the general progress tone.
Runtime users map Disabled to Danger. Preserve a security or access restriction's meaning; do not convert every 'Disabled' label to Neutral automatically.
Documented drift is not an approved exception. Product implementation, Figma reconciliation, and final design approval remain separate adoption work.
notes: This is a proposed status contract from the FlowX DS Gap Audit of September 4, 2026 (adoption item #1), not a shipped product API. Colors are FlowX palette tokens; typography matches existing soft tags. Sizes, paired foreground colors, icon scale, and the dark treatment are a proposed consolidation, not a Figma extraction.

Heights are minimums (min-height), not fixed heights. Small resolves to 2 + 16 + 2 = 20px and Medium to 4 + 16 + 4 = 24px for a single-line label; the pill grows vertically when a long or translated label wraps.

The rendered documentation component sets display: inline-flex on the container, overriding the spec helper's display: flex; padding is applied as paddingY paddingX shorthand and the fill comes from the tone/surface background token with no stroke.
The spec describes the label font as Open Sans; the rendered component applies it through the site font variable var(--font-flowx).

The five tone names double as the component's documented states. Hover, pressed, selected, focused, and disabled interaction states do not exist by design; 'Disabled' may still be a resource's visible label.
gaps: No Figma link and no Figma-extracted node data exist for this component; nothing here comes from the Vibma pipeline.
The spec defines no decisionLog, considerations, or knownExceptions.
No border or stroke is defined on either surface (the pill is explicitly borderless), so there is no dark-surface border token to record.
Icon stroke weight is not part of the spec; the Phosphor 'bold' weight is only what the documentation preview renders.
No numeric maximum label length or truncation rule is defined beyond the guidance to prefer one to three words and let the pill grow.
No spacing token is cited for the 4px gap, 8px/12px horizontal padding, or 2px/4px vertical padding; the sources give raw pixel values only.
No focus ring, hover, pressed, or disabled colors exist because the component defines no interaction states.
